problem: On REVERIE (high-level instruction navigation plus remote object grounding), prior work reuses fine-grained VLN agents with a simple trainable language encoder and an interactive pointer module. These do not capture high-level semantics or commonsense, and they use no structured memory.
motivation: High-level instructions give weak guidance, so humans form an overview of what and where the target is and keep matching the current scene against it. The paper imitates this by pre-training vision-language grounding models for scene and object matching and adding memory of past states.
key_idea: Pre-train ViLBERT-based Scene Grounding (which viewpoint matches the instruction) and Object Grounding (which object matches) models, use them as encoders in a memory-augmented attentive action decoder, and fuse their scores with action logits at inference.
insight: Ablations show the gain does not come from BERT-style structure alone. A ViLBERT encoder without Scene Grounding pre-training (exp. 3) gets Val Unseen RG SPL 4.84, versus 7.31 with the Scene Grounding encoder (exp. 6). The viewpoint-based ViLPointer (unseen RGS 67.45 vs MattNet 56.63) captures cross-view object relations. The memory adds success at the cost of longer paths, and 3 memory blocks work best. Summing action, scene and object logits shortens trajectories.
method: Scene Grounding task: 5-way multiple-choice ViLBERT fine-tuning on (instruction, 36-view ResNet-152 viewpoint) pairs. The positive is the end viewpoint, a hard negative is the second-to-last viewpoint, and the other negatives are random. Score = W2(h_CLS ⊙ h_IMG), trained with cross-entropy.

Object Grounding task: ViLBERT pre-trained first on single-image box grounding (67k samples), then on viewpoint-based grounding over all Mask R-CNN boxes at the target viewpoint (4.4k samples), with IoU>0.5 labels; object score is averaged over boxes sharing an id.

ViLEncoder / ViLPointer: the Scene Grounding ViLBERT plus a BiLSTM gives instruction features grounded in the current panorama. The Object Grounding ViLBERT scores boxes in each navigable view, and top-k averaged features are appended to the navigable view feature.

Memory-augmented decoder: each step stores s_t = FC([a_{t-1}, attentive visual feature]) in an addressable memory. N_mem self-attention Transformer blocks over memory and N_state cross-attention blocks give s_t^a, which feeds an LSTM together with the grounded text and navigable view features. Action logits come from attention over the navigable views.
Inference logit fusion: navigation uses the cumulative sum over steps of action logits, object grounding scores and scene grounding scores. The final box comes from ViLPointer at the stop viewpoint.
Training: imitation (cross-entropy plus progress monitor) plus RL with ±3 reward (stop within 3 m of the target viewpoint), all loss weights 1, 13000 iterations, max 40 steps.

setting.backbone: ViLBERT (BERT-base language stream, pre-trained on Conceptual Captions + 12 tasks, fine-tuned) + BiLSTM + LSTM/Transformer memory decoder
setting.training_data: REVERIE train (59 scenes, 10466 instructions); Scene Grounding set of 10312 samples; Object Grounding sets of 67432 (image) and 4356 (viewpoint) samples; ViLBERT pre-trained on Conceptual Captions and 12 vision-language tasks
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views, ResNet-152 features) plus annotated object boxes (Mask R-CNN features)
setting.privileged: GT annotated object bounding boxes at each viewpoint are given as input (REVERIE setting)

numbers.evidence: Table 2, comparison with SOTA on REVERIE, Ours Val Seen

results: The model beats the REVERIE baseline on every split. On val-unseen, SR is 31.53 vs 14.40, RGS 22.41 vs 7.84 and RGSPL 11.56 vs 4.67. On test, RGS is 19.02 vs 11.28 and RGSPL 9.20 vs 6.08. It remains far below humans (test RGS 77.84).
limitations: Large seen-unseen gap, and long navigation paths (unseen TL about 41-49 m).
Heavy pipeline (several ViLBERT models, Mask R-CNN features) and uses GT annotated object boxes.
Localization failures from ambiguous referents and relative-position reasoning.
